title: Online identity theft - distinguishing it from regular fraud
p1: Most people think online identity theft and fraud are the same thing. They aren't. That small difference can determine whether a stolen credit card is your biggest problem or just the beginning of a much larger one.
p2: Regular fraud is usually about stealing your money. Online identity theft is about stealing you. Someone may collect your personal details, create accounts in your name, apply for loans, or even reset passwords to take over your digital life. The financial loss is often only one part of the damage. Your reputation, credit, and access to important accounts can also be affected.
p3: A useful way to remember it is this: fraud targets your wallet, while identity theft targets your identity. That's why checking bank statements alone isn't enough. Review your credit reports, turn on multi-factor authentication, and be cautious about sharing personal details online. Many people discover identity theft weeks or months after it starts because no money disappeared at first.
conclusion: Before today, did you think identity theft was simply another name for fraud, or have you ever seen an example where someone's identity was misused without their money being stolen right away?
